videos.title: Holding the guitar without fighting it
videos.description: Strap height, wrist angle, and a thumb that stays calm.

notes.abstract: Comfortable hold beats “perfect textbook” if it lets you play longer.
points: Raise the neck slightly so fretting stays easy.
Check strap height standing and sitting.
notes.conclusion: Pain in the first ten minutes is setup, not toughness.

videos.title: Open chords that actually change
videos.description: Slow switches with common shapes: G, C, D, Em, Am.

notes.abstract: Chord changes improve when you move the guide finger first and land together.
points: Isolate the hardest switch and loop it.
Mute and place before you strum.
Use a metronome only after placements are clean.
notes.conclusion: Fast wrong changes become permanent — slow correct ones scale up.

videos.title: Strumming that keeps time
videos.description: Down-up patterns with a quiet right hand and steady pulse.

notes.abstract: Strumming is timekeeping first, decoration second.
points: Lock a downstroke on the beat.
Add ups only when downs are steady.
Mute strings lightly if fretting is still noisy.
notes.conclusion: If the song rushes, simplify the pattern before blaming the left hand.

videos.title: Barre chords without the death grip
videos.description: Partial barres and arm weight so the index finger does not squeeze alone.

notes.abstract: Barres work better with arm weight and placement than with raw squeeze.
points: Roll the index slightly onto its side edge.
Bring the elbow in to add weight.
Build from partial barres before full ones.
notes.conclusion: A numb fretting hand means too much force — reset lighter.

videos.title: Lead lines that sing
videos.description: Target notes, phrasing spaces, and why endless notes get boring.

notes.abstract: Memorable lead playing aims at strong notes and leaves air.
points: Choose chord tones as landing spots.
Repeat a motif before inventing a new one.
notes.conclusion: More notes is not more music — clearer targets are.

resorts.name: First-month song set
resorts.summary: Three songs that teach changes without crushing motivation.
resorts.intro:
Pick songs with mostly open chords and slow tempos.

Rotate: one comfort song, one stretch song, one rhythm drill.

Record weekly so progress is visible.

resorts.name: String & neck care
resorts.summary: Wipe-down, humidity basics, and when to change strings.
resorts.intro:
Wipe strings after playing. Avoid extreme dryness or damp storage.

Change strings when tone dulls or tuning becomes unstable — not only when they snap.
